source: Daily Investment Brief Macroeconomic Dashboard + authoritative-source supplementation
sourceStatus: Daily Investment Brief remains the primary dashboard layer, but automated retrieval still exposes client-side placeholders ('Analyzing...' / '--'). No values are inferred from placeholders. MacroMicro remains supplemental where accessible. Current gaps are filled with official ISM/EIA/Federal Reserve data, company filings/earnings and current Reuters/SEMI market evidence. The retired legacy macro dashboard is not used.
methodology: Directional channels are scored from -2 to +2. Dashboard readings are inputs, not trading signals. Creator/video/social claims have zero direct score weight until independently verified. Company-specific AI orders/backlog raise the AI-capex channel but do not mechanically reclassify broad consumer/growth conditions.
regime: Bifurcated stagflationary expansion: refined-product inflation and elevated global long-end yields are squeezing consumers and long-duration assets, while verified AI infrastructure demand is accelerating across servers, custom accelerators, networking, memory and data platforms. The AI bottleneck is broadening from compute alone into memory bandwidth/data movement, power and financing.

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.regime: Broad demand mixed; AI demand accelerating
channels.interpretation: Broad growth is not accelerating cleanly: hiring and petroleum demand are softening. In parallel, Dell/Broadcom/HPE/Credo/Snowflake show a genuine AI investment and consumption boom. Treat this as a bifurcated economy rather than a broad-growth upgrade.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.regime: Oil inflation keeps hike risk elevated despite weaker hiring
channels.interpretation: Weak hiring increases two-sided policy risk, but $90+ crude and extreme product cracks keep the Fed's inflation constraint active.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.interpretation: A US 10Y around 4.8% and high real yields keep the discount-rate hurdle severe. Strong AI earnings can overpower this at the company level, but expensive/distant cash flows remain vulnerable.

channels.label: Broad Credit
channels.interpretation: Large quality issuers can finance AI buildout, but high risk-free rates make capital efficiency, customer funding and cash conversion increasingly important.

channels.label: Weak-End Credit Stress
channels.interpretation: Weak borrowers still face punitive refinancing conditions even as hyperscalers and high-quality AI suppliers access capital. The credit split reinforces quality selection.

channels.label: Consumer
channels.interpretation: High fuel/product prices, borrowing costs and slower hiring pressure financed discretionary demand. AI capex strength does not remove the household squeeze.

channels.label: Housing
channels.interpretation: A 10Y around 4.8% keeps mortgage affordability and leveraged property activity under pressure.

channels.label: Industrial / AI / Power Capex
channels.regime: Verified AI infrastructure boom inside mixed economy
channels.interpretation: Dell's $60.9B quarterly AI orders and $95B backlog, Broadcom's accelerator/networking outlook, HPE's Cloud & AI growth and Credo's >100% revenue growth materially strengthen evidence of funded AI capex. Power, networking, memory and systems are all seeing real demand.

channels.label: AI Memory / Bandwidth
channels.regime: Memory wall + constrained supply + architecture co-design
channels.interpretation: DDR5/DDR4/NAND constraints, HBM capacity competition and accelerating interconnect needs show memory/data movement becoming a first-order AI bottleneck. SEMICON Taiwan is shifting the discussion toward HBM4, CXL, 3D stacking, near/in-memory computing and tighter compute-memory co-design.

channels.label: Input Costs
channels.regime: Energy, memory, component and freight inflation extreme
channels.interpretation: Energy/products remain extreme while memory and electronic components are constrained. Pricing-power suppliers benefit; server/system vendors must manage component cost, inventory and supply agreements.

channels.label: Labour
channels.interpretation: ADP private payrolls rose only 38k in August and ISM Manufacturing Employment slowed. AI investment strength is not yet translating into broad labour acceleration.

channels.label: Risk Appetite
channels.regime: High dispersion; semis/memory bid, software fragile
channels.interpretation: Headline indices are choppy, but earnings are driving sharp internal rotation toward semiconductors/memory and away from duration-heavy software. This is selective risk appetite, not broad risk-on.

channels.label: Crude
channels.interpretation: Brent settled $95.63 and WTI $91.01 while EIA crude stocks fell 4.5M barrels. Lower product supplied warns that high prices are suppressing demand.

channels.label: Refined Products
channels.interpretation: European gasoline/diesel margins remain extreme while US refinery utilisation is already near max. Product scarcity remains the strongest current energy-inflation channel.

channels.label: US Gas / Global LNG
channels.regime: Global security premium with US feedgas advantage
channels.interpretation: European gas remains elevated as buyers seek secure supply. US LNG/take-or-pay infrastructure retains strategic value.

channels.label: Gold / Monetary Hedge
channels.regime: Structural hedge intact; high real yields cap tactical upside
channels.interpretation: Gold remains structurally supported by fiscal/geopolitical risk but high real rates and a firm dollar still argue for staged exposure.
